_source: Captured 2026-09-10 from www.imperva.com by curl, byte counts cross-checked against a same-origin fetch run from inside a live page on that origin (2513 / 554 / 6223 / 1804). These are the real bytes behind the field report where a crawl of /products/ found 33 pages and a manual pass found 43.

_whyThisMatters.robots: 21 Sitemap: lines across several User-agent blocks, wrapped in Yoast '# START/END BLOCK' comments, and containing a bare 'Disallow:' with no value. Ranking must put /products/sitemap_index.xml first for a /products/ base.
_whyThisMatters.pageSitemap: 41 <url> entries, 41 <loc>, zero image:loc. 17 are deep /products/data-security/* pages a nav-only link crawl cannot see.
_whyThisMatters.modalSitemap: 8 <url> entries but NINE <loc> matches — cds-demo-popup carries a nested <image:image><image:loc> pointing at an .svg. A <loc> regex that allows any namespace prefix audits that asset as a page. This is why the parser strips media subtrees first, and it was caught by these real bytes rather than by a hand-written fixture.
_whyThisMatters.htmlWhereXmlExpected: A real 200 response whose body is HTML, truncated to 3KB. A sitemap parser that only counts <loc> calls this an EMPTY sitemap instead of saying the response was not XML. Bot interstitials (Imperva's own 'Pardon Our Interruption') are the same class: 200 + HTML. The assertion is about the class, not the vendor.
